sections.what_happened: (a) Trump announced 'Project Freedom' Sunday: US will guide stranded neutral ships out of the Strait of Hormuz starting Monday, warned interference would be 'dealt with forcefully'; WSJ (via bankbit): coordination process through countries/insurers/shipping orgs, NO US warship escorts; Axios (via bankbit): US Navy ships 'in the vicinity' + will share unmined-lane info; CENTCOM (via Al Jazeera mirrors): supports with 15,000 personnel, 100+ aircraft, warships, drones. (b) NYT (Sunday): US military has secretly guided ~70 commercial vessels through the strait over past 3 weeks despite Trump's April suspension of the original Project Freedom (suspended <48h after April announcement when Saudi Arabia refused Prince Sultan Air Base/airspace use). (c) Iran military Monday (via Al Jazeera mirrors + Indian outlets): 'Any foreign armed force, especially the aggressive US Army, will be attacked if they attempt to approach and enter the Strait of Hormuz'; lawmaker Ebrahim Azizi: any US interference = violation of ceasefire. (d) Fars: two missiles hit a US warship at southern end of the strait; CENTCOM/US denied. (e) UKMTO (Sunday): cargo ship attacked by multiple small craft near the strait; ~2 dozen attacks in/around strait since war began. ~1,600-2,000 vessels stranded in the Gulf; pre-war transit ~100-150 ships/day now <10.
sections.what_verified: Multiple independent mirrors (bankbit, edgeone x3, thenationalnews context) converge on the Sunday announcement + Monday Iranian warning. UKMTO confirms shipping attacks pattern.
sections.what_disputed: US/CENTCOM denied the Fars warship-hit claim. Edgeone mirrors have date-confusion issues (recycled May content) — the (c) statement needs an IRNA/ISNA direct citation.
sections.why_matters: Trump starts his Hormuz 'rescue' today — Tehran just told the US Navy to stay out or be hit. The Fars missile claim (US-denied) is the live-wire.
sections.context: Background: Strait of Hormuz — Trump (re)launches 'Project Freedom' ship-guiding mission Monday; Iran warns US Navy it will be attacked if it enters the strait; Fars claims missiles hit US warship, CENTCOM denies

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump starts his Hormuz 'rescue' today — Tehran just told the US Navy to stay out or be hit. The Fars missile claim (US-denied) is the live-wire. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Humanitarian rescue mission for 2,000 stranded crews — or a US pretext to force a naval showdown at Hormuz? Comment sections (35K-like CENTCOM reel, 4.5K comments) split between 'full control' believers, Iranian-side celebrators ('American ships fled'), and AI/propaganda skeptics; pocketbook undercurrent: gas prices.
